output.summary: Approved G1033 design revision 2: the Claude marketplace build rendered the 'official' channel for 0.0.0-dev builds, so package_status() reported a false skill-metadata mismatch with a Codex hint. One shared channel_for_version() rule is used by the build and the check (release bundles stay byte-identical); install_harness() picks a Claude, Codex or neutral reinstall hint from the install path. Tests build the marketplace and run full validate, asserting no `plugin package` entry and no 'skill discovery metadata' (git/gh entries ignored), plus a negative case; the test runs on all platforms. Review approved after one round. After merge, rebuild and update the installed Claude caches.

responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: every environment == [] assertion is replaced by a package-check-only assertion. No environment entry may start with `plugin package` (covering both cli.package_check failure forms), and none may contain `skill discovery metadata`. The SKILL.md channel and policy-entry assertions stay, and a negative case checks that the assertion fires on a wrong-channel build. A fake gh on PATH was considered and not chosen. Notes taken: the test runs via sys.executable zzzops.py and is added to NATIVE_COVERAGE; exact-dict package_status() assertions are grepped at implement; a comment explains why `<m>` (the cache segment, which is the marketplace.json name) is used.

output.summary: Revision 2 answers review_design:1:1. Tests no longer assert environment == [], because validate's environment also carries git and gh checks, and CI has no token. They assert that no entry starts with `plugin package` and that `skill discovery metadata` is absent. They also keep the SKILL.md channel and policy-entry checks, and add a negative case proving the assertion can fail. The new bundle test runs through zzzops.py and joins NATIVE_COVERAGE, the `<m>` derivation is commented, and implement greps for exact-dict package_status() assertions. Cause and fix are unchanged: one shared channel_for_version for build and check, plus a path-based install_harness() for a Claude/Codex/neutral reinstall hint.

Generated Claude marketplaces no longer fail their own package self-check. The bundle builder now renders skill metadata with package.channel_for_version, the rule package_status uses, so a 0.0.0-dev build claims the development channel. The self-check failure hint now names the installing harness, detected from the install location: Claude Code with the marketplace update and plugin update commands, Codex, or a neutral line naming both. Claude acceptance runs the full validate from the generated marketplace and the installed cache and fails on any plugin package entry, and the Claude marketplace and maintaining docs describe the rule.

findings.text: The planned assertion `environment == []` also checks gh, so it would fail in CI. validate's environment is check_environment(git) + gh_problems(s) + package_check() (cli.py:194-202), and gh_problems reports 'gh is not installed' or 'gh is not authenticated: run `gh auth login`, or set GH_TOKEN' (gh.py:72-81). The validate-linux and validate-claude jobs export no GitHub token, and dev machines may lack gh. So the new test_marketplace_bundle test and the claude_plugin_acceptance checks would fail even with the fix. The design's local reproduction passed only because gh is authenticated on this machine. Fix: assert that no environment entry starts with 'plugin package:' and that 'skill discovery metadata' is absent (simplest, and works on every platform), or put a fake gh (.agents/engine_fake_gh.py) on PATH. Keep the SKILL.md channel and policy-entry assertions.

output.summary: Approved. review_design:1:1 is resolved: the tests now assert only that no environment entry starts with 'plugin package' and none contains 'skill discovery metadata'. That prefix covers both package_check failure forms (cli.py:242-249), and gh and git entries are ignored, so the tests pass in CI without a token. A wrong-channel negative case proves the assertion can fire and that the hint names Claude Code. All three notes were taken: the test is in NATIVE_COVERAGE and runs via sys.executable zzzops.py; exact-dict package_status assertions are grepped at implement; a comment explains the <m> segment. No new findings.

Approved with no findings. package.py matches design revision 2. channel_for_version is shared by the build and the check. _is_codex_cachebuster is extracted unchanged. install_harness follows the design's order (cachebuster, Claude base, Codex base, generated catalog, None) with resolved bases and a guard for a missing home. _cache_marketplace documents <m> and falls back to zzzops. The hint has a Claude, Codex and neutral form, and harness is on both dicts while package_check still reads only ok and detail. The build script passes the shared channel. Release bundles at 2.0.0 are byte-identical between b452cd7 and a1d408f apart from zzzops/package.py itself (74 files). The acceptance helper checks the report shape and ignores gh and git entries, and it is called on the generated and the installed runtime in a prepared project. The docs are updated. Outside the diff, no other caller depends on the old hint text or on an exact package_status key set.

findings.text: The second recorded command runs all of CI's Linux validation, not what proves this goal. With no shard arguments, `python .github/scripts/run_product_validation.py --platform linux` takes linux_validation(): (1) `unittest discover -s .agents` over the entire suite (about 600 test methods, more than 1,300 ids), serially in one process, where CI uses 8 shards x 2 workers; (2) `npm run test:plugin` and `npm run test:release`, which need Node and node_modules from `npm ci`, so network on a fresh worktree; (3) prompt_stats --check and compileall. run_tests runs every recorded command, so this makes it slow and environment-dependent, and a failure anywhere in the repository fails this goal. Command 1 already covers the changed modules, and test_ci_selection checks the new native ids against NATIVE_COVERAGE. The full suite is dev-required-tests' job. Fix: drop the second command. If a selection-wiring cross-check is wanted, add a fast offline one such as `python -c "import runpy; m=runpy.run_path('.github/scripts/run_product_validation.py'); m['select_native_tests'](m['discover_native_tests']())"`.

output.summary: Approved. review_tests:1:1 is resolved: the full run_product_validation --platform linux command is replaced by the offline select_native_tests(discover_native_tests()) check, which runs in 0.11 s from the worktree root and raises on a missing, duplicate or empty id. Command 1 run from the worktree root fails only for the expected pre-implementation reasons (76 tests, 5 failures and 9 errors, none environmental). The new source-level test that acceptance main() calls require_no_package_check at least twice fails today as intended; it is weak against a call in a comment, but acceptable as defence in depth.

spec:
Found while designing G1003 (2026-11-01). `zzzops validate`, run from the Claude marketplace cache built by .github/scripts/build_claude_plugin.py (zzzops-claude-marketplace-c3791a0-20261101) on a fresh clone of another repository, reported `environment: "plugin package: skill discovery metadata does not match the plugin build: skills/add-zzzops-goal/SKILL.md; reinstall ZzzOps from its Codex marketplace."`. A correct Claude install must not report a mismatch, and the hint must name the harness the plugin was installed for.

Find why the Claude build's SKILL.md differs from what the package check expects (build step rewriting the file, or the check assuming the Codex bundle), fix it, and make the reinstall hint harness-aware.

Acceptance: a test builds the Claude marketplace (as CI's installed-cache acceptance does) and runs validate from it with no environment error; the hint names Claude or Codex correctly; docs/design edits if the contract changes.
title: Claude installs report a false skill-metadata mismatch with a Codex reinstall hint
